articles.title: Follow The Star Signs
articles.subtitle: How I turned Spiritual Enlightenment into Profit
articles.bodyHtml:
I've always held one firm belief:

To be successful is to know yourself. 

That belief has guided me throughout my life and it is precisely why I decided to embark on a spiritual journey to India last year in search of myself.

I grabbed my finest Tom Ford sunglasses, picked out a suitable Rolex and packed two suitcases to the brim with an assortment of flowing shirts, linen trousers and, of course, a couple of expensive fine suits. After all, a rule of thumb that I learnt from my time at the Kensington-upon-Thames-upon-Cladbury University is that one must always be prepared for when business opportunities strikes.

The interests alone from my previous successful investments paid for my plane ticket (and a couple of margaritas), but despite the joyous occasion of travelling first class, I found myself feeling rather sombre.

I had observed a worrying trend of investments generating considerably less profit than they ought to. Environmentalism was on the rise, consumer spending was declining and the economic market was being beaten down by the Woke crowd, who insisted that Less is More.

I am well aware that I am just another white, middle-aged man, but I still possess a young mind with a lot of elasticity. Naturally, I was willing of course to conduct some research of my own and approach these ideas with an open mind.

Perhaps it was true. Perhaps the constant materialistic pursuit of possessions was not quite as positive as it seemed. Perhaps the Woke crowd was onto something, albeit pursuing it in such a clumsy manner that they were tanking economies around the world.

Perhaps I could step in and restore the balance, if only I could first find balance within myself.

Over the course of several days, I went on to experience a multitude of spiritual activities. I attended a sunrise yoga session in Rishikesh, visited the Taj Mahal, underwent multiple purification rituals and Ayurvedic spa treatments and slept upon the finest satin sheets money could buy in hotels around Jaipur, their sandalwood-scented lobbies invigorating both body and mind.

After a week and a couple of days, I was truly living like one of the locals.

And just like that, opportunity struck.

I was sitting cross-legged in an exclusive smoking lounge, enjoying both a hookah and a smoky whiskey, contemplating the fact that money and power really do mean everything in this world.

After all, here I was, in a supposedly alcohol-free establishment, enjoying one of the most soul-soothing whiskies I had ever tasted, solely because I had generously tipped the personnel.

It was then that a wealthy Indian businessman decided to join me.

We discussed economic models, business ventures and the considerable wealth that certain noble and aristocratic Indian families were sitting on, unwilling to reinvest it into the economy.

"If only Lord Brihaspati would guide us," my new Indian business friend exclaimed.

I leaned back, deep in thought and looked up at the night sky above us, at the sea of stars looking back down at me.

It was at that precise moment, beneath the celestial canopy of the Indian night (likely aided by the buzz of the whisky in my system), that I experienced what can only be described as a revelation.

What if we could convince millions of Indian investors that the answers to their questions about shares, stakes and portfolios were literally in the stars?

My like-minded friend and I spent the remainder of that week conjuring up a package we could sell to these investors, backed by grandiose stories of wishes coming true, of Indian gurus investing a single rupee and turning it into millions.

We named our venture Celestial Capital Partners™, an exclusive financial advisory service, combining the ancient wisdom of the heavens with the sophisticated economic principles I had mastered during my time at Kensington-upon-Thames-upon-Cladbury University.

Naturally, that expertise would be offered for a modest consultation fee, followed by an annual management fee to ensure that our clients received their uninterrupted celestial guidance. The finer details of the arrangement were rather complicated, but our investors were delighted by the possibilities and we as well by the financial returns.

It was easy to dismiss any scepticism or concerns surrounding our business proposal. No serious economist could ever guarantee the success of an investments with 100% certainty and it would be foolish to claim otherwise, celestial intervention or not. The markets, much like the universe itself, are unpredictable.
Yet we could most certainly assure anyone who doubted us that Jupiter had smiled most favourably upon our enterprise and we had concrete, quantifiable financial data to back up our claims.

I returned home, skin tanned, spirituality renewed, pockets loaded with money, a perfect white bright smile and a newfound optimistic outlook on the future. I had set out to find myself and what I found was something I had possessed all along.

So remember, dear reader, the universe does not simply hand out opportunities. One must possess the foresight to recognize them, the courage to pursue them and, preferably, a sufficiently diversified portfolio.

Namaste.

articles.description: What began as a journey of spiritual self-discovery in India became an extraordinary business opportunity for our financial columnist Thaddeus R. Pinchpenny. Combining the spirituality of India with modern investment strategies, Pinchpenny recounts how an unexpected opportunity led to the founding of Celestial Capital Partners™ and how that endeavour has turned out to be very lucrative.

articles.title: The Unfortunate Plucked Chicken Incident and the Decline of Public Decency
articles.bodyHtml:
It is easy to turn on the evening news, open any newspaper or, for the modern, sophisticated readers out there, open up your screens and click on your favourite digital magazine, only to find yourself disheartened by the state of the world.



We live in such polarized, Big Brother-like societies nowadays that no one is safe from the watchful eyes of cellular devices, available in every hand and pocket. Not even the people in the upper echelons of society are exempt from this type of surveillance, which is mind-boggling.

Gone are the old days of chaperones and spokespersons, who were most often the only form of contact between the rest of the world and our esteemed Royals, unless they themselves chose to make a public appearance.

Please do not mistake my nostalgia for times past for naiveté. I am well aware that there has always been a very particular breed of paparazzi who push things too far, but I must say that this mortifying behaviour has become far more prevalent in modern times. 

There is no such thing as discretion and dignity anymore. 

The media as well as the public and young people on their Social Media platforms are obsessed with scrutinizing every little action, no matter how innocent, of celebrities and, no less, members of the Royal family.

The so crudely named internet phenomenon, "The Chicken Incident", has exploded online these past few days. Young girls with egos as inflated as their lips and bosoms are expressing their squawking opinions on what constitutes animal endangerment, claiming that all royal people are "evil" or "narcissistic spoiled bastards" (or some tired repetition of those words). I cannot help but chuckle in disbelief at these incoherent arguments floating about in their echo chambers.

And for those of you who, like me, do not live on the interwebs and have been caught unaware and out of the loop, let me quickly tell you exactly what this "Chicken Incident" entails.  

Our dear young prince, Thomas Irvington Chad the Second, was caught on film when he found a lost chicken, carefully took it into his arms and went on to find a cool place in the shade, where he proceeded to remove some of its feathers with an innocent smile on his face. 

The chicken was a Cochin chicken with beautiful, golden and fluffy feathers. No doubt our dear young prince wanted to pick out a few of the softest and most beautiful ones to bring back to his mother, the Queen.

And now, for this action, he is scrutinized and subjected to hatred. 

Now, don't misunderstand me. Of course, I don't think it is right to pluck a live chicken, even one with such an impressive plumage. But we need to show grace toward young royals who have lived sheltered life, who abide by rules and etiquette that differs from those of the common people and who have most likely never needed to associate themselves with simple farm animals. 

It is unfortunate that this simple mistake should now taint his image forever on the interwebs, thanks to the negative harping of thousands, if not millions, of people who are unable to show any forgiveness or compassion, simply because of his status.

I've heard the discourse many times now. People deem his action horrific and cruel simply because he was a bit overenthusiastic when he laughed. 

And that young man certainly has a charming boisterous laugh! 

Is he to be villainized because of this? 

There are also many images emerging of the chicken flailing about, shaking off the last remnants of feathers on its body and screaming its head off. Nowhere do we see that it was the young prince who plucked every last feather clean off the chicken.

It was simply an unfortunate escalation, driven by that tiny little bird-brain, which, in every sense did make, as the Swedes express it, "a chicken out of a feather" (pardon my pun) and rendered itself completely featherless because it acted as one would expect of a dumb, poor fowl?

Are we to condemn this young man for life for this? 

The chicken has since been collected by the farmer and is undergoing rehabilitation, which is proceeding quite well. The fowl has been given a lovely little sweater, still lays eggs as normal and was seen on last night's news pecking about the ground together with its fellow feathered friends, happy as can be. 

Does that sound like an animal that has been subjected to severe and malicious abuse?

That chicken was found by our young prince wandering around the premises of a golf course where he was playing. It could have been a far more dire situation for the poor chicken if any golf balls had struck it (an errant birdie, for example) and if that had been the prince's ballm then he would most certainly have gotten in trouble for that as well. 

So when do we blame the farmer? When do we point fingers at the farmer for not securing the perimeters of his poultry farm and allowing one of his birds to escape? Is it only because it wasn't caught on tape that it didn't happen in the eyes of the modern media? 

We could go on and on about this but I think I've made my point.

Now, as a final statement, I wish to extend my outmost heartfelt apologies to the Royal Family. 

May you stand steadfast in this storm. 

May God Save the queen and may I wish our dear young prince, Thomas Irvington Chad the Second, a very happy 42nd birthday.

Godspeed.

articles.title: The Death of Corporate Accountability and the Novel That Could Save Western Civilization
articles.bodyHtml:
We've all heard the chantings of the people out in the streets these past few days, a red-hot anger that seeps through our pavements, cobblestones and zebra crossings. We, as a society, have been shown yet again that corporations are above the laws-- laws that should be the foundation of our country, laws that should carry us all on their calloused, muscle-y shoulders and make us proud of how far we have come as a civilization.

It makes you want to weep, fall to your knees, shake your fist to the skies and exclaim, "Why?!"

I can envision the top shots behind Arbule Corp. standing in their tall glass towers, clinking glasses, laughing and both literally and figuratively looking down at the masses parading outside their headquarters. What can they do? What power do they have to overthrow the leaders and visionaries behind this corrupt corporation when they are the ones calling the shots?

"In its majestic equality, the law forbids rich and poor alike to sleep under bridges, beg in the streets and steal loaves of bread."
— Anatole France, The Red Lily (1894), Chapter VII.

We could have an endless debate, going around in circles like fish in an ever-lowering pond, until we lie there in the sludge and mud, gasping for air and wiggling helplessly under the scorching sun, arguing about the positives and negatives of tort reform.
We all know this is going nowhere.

Now, imagine that there was a book-- a book of the highest intellectual caliber, with knowledge and truths between every page, that could end this debate once and for all.

The Holy Grail. A myth.

Imagine.

What if I told you that this myth, a myth of great importance, like the Round Table of King Arthur's court or Emperors Nero's own fiddle-- still smelling of smoke, a witness to the Great Fire of Rome in 64 AD, was no myth at all?

I truly believe that my book (yes!) could unite us again and overthrow the capitalist pigs in their glass towers. The old, dried but truthful ink of my old trusty typewriter, an enigma of machinery that has borne witness to countless heralded articles, read and loved by many, has been clacking away at this book for years. Its manuscript pages have almost yellowed with age, but the content remains just as fresh and young as the day.

I am well aware that I am teasing you, my dear reader(s), but alas, I cannot yet reveal the truth. Not without first finding a publisher who actually values the truth, who can see the raw contents and fully understand them just as they are, without endless pleading to change the meaning, erase the core of what the book is trying to convey, or censor what I believe is my life's greatest accomplishment.

And for that, I am afraid that the rage of the people will need to carry on for a while longer.

I will end this article with yet another quote that I find fitting to my situation,

"If liberty means anything at all it means the right to tell people what they do not want to hear."
— George Orwell, The Freedom of the Press, his proposed preface to Animal Farm (written 1945, published 1972)
articles.description: As public anger intensifies over corporate greed and the erosion of accountability, our columnist Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar examines the feelings of the general public, the limitations of tort reform and the extraordinary literary work that may hold the key to restoring peace to the Western civilization.

articles.title: The Silent Infiltration: How Communist Ideology Threatens Our Way of Life
articles.bodyHtml:
The dinner table, a scene that sparks joy and a sense of home for millions of people in our beautiful nation. The familiarity of the wooden surface, the soft clinking of cutlery and glasses, crinkling decorated tissues and the warm embrace of breaking bread amongst friends and family. 

A place that should feel safe.

Where we should be able to relax.
     To let the hectic and stressful day leave your
           shoulders and satisfying food enter your belly.

That safety has been taken from me.

It was a normal evening, just like the previous evening and the evenings before. I was seated at our grand oak table, candles lit, wine glasses filled and the vibrating expectancy of a juicy savoury steak being served in front of me.

But that moment never came. 

Instead, I was served a cold bowl, its bland, green content completely odourless, nothing to stimulate my culinary senses or enrich my mind. My husband smiled at me with an expectant look in his eyes, as if to say, "Gaze upon this glorious dish!" My knuckles whitening and the cutlery in my hand creaking and bending in my concealed wrath, I took a long, hard look at the man before me. 

For you see, Communism has infiltrated my dinner table. 

It had started slowly.
Short, innocent ads playing in our living room, depicting people cutting vegetables, chewing on carrot sticks and rows of perfect white teeth smiling while selling their products and promoting this lifestyle. Slowly it turned more sinister. A recent released documentary depicting the alleged horrors of the meat industry and the mass hysteria of munching grass instead of the grass-fed animals themselves spread like a wildfire throughout our nation. Banners, protesters and vegans en masse began hounding the everyday Joe and Jane, claiming more and more victims. 

It is preposterous! Humans have, since the time of our Lord and Saviour's birth, eaten meat, digesting the valuable nutrients that are required to make our bodies and muscles strong. Have we all suddenly forgotten that meat is an incredible source of protein? 

How are we, as a nation, supposed to be able to protect ourselves if our bodies wither away, the butcher and hunting industries collapse and with them the economy? Who could benefit from this?
The answer has been right in front of everyones eyes: a big glaring C from across our nation's borders, a tsunami waiting to happen. 

How do we stop this infiltration and the risk it poses to our nation's security? I throw my hands in the air; I have to admit and be honest here: I don't know. 

But I do know that it begins with the simple word "no."

And that was exactly what I told my husband, the bowl of grass turned upside down and laying on the floor. 

No.

articles.title: Why Must Every Period Drama Be So Unnecessarily Historical?
articles.bodyHtml:
Girls, let's be real here.

Have you ever opened up a history book, looked at the 3D-generated depictions of what the ancient ruins of old building used to look like, bustling with life and ordinary everyday scenes from days gone by, or at the black-and-white or sepia-toned photographs of stern and, in many cases, quite frankly plain and unfortunate-looking people who may have been our great-great-grandfathers and grandmothers and thought,
"Wow, I wish I lived back then".

Maybe you have, but as soon as you think about it for more than a couple of seconds, the thought of having to travel on foot along hot, dusty roads in flat, ugly sandals, with no access to warm bathwater or even proper plumbing, should be enough to make you go,
"No way!"

Right?!

So please, WHY is it that there's a new period drama coming out in theaters near you every week? Or that whenever I scroll through my streaming services, I see the annoying little banner saying "Recommended for you" with three, four, FIVE little preview images of ladies in big wigs, frilly crinolines and those hideous hundred-buttons boots coyly poking out from underneath their skirts?

I am sick and tired of the recycled historical events such as the American Revolutionary War , the French Revolution (see a pattern here?) and various films about royalty or the women's rights movement during the Victorian or Elizabethan era, like, grow up!

We do not need yet another re-enactment of Pride & Prejudice with chaste hand-holding and kisses. We live in a modern era! We demand sloppy, toe-curling erotic action. Is that not feminist enough for you?

I review movies, shows, musicals and other types of media for a living and let me tell you, there is nothing as unsexy as the knowledge that Mr. Chiselled Jaw-Handsome the Third is probably smelling of unwashed armpits, poopy arse mixed with ink fumes (because many people in the old days used to wipe with newspaper articles because there was no such thing as toilet paper!!!) and days-old musty man-sweat.

Would it be so wrong to show me a hot, full-frontal shower scene set in an immaculately decorated Victorian bathroom so that I could at least pretend that they all actually smell nice?

Or those silly outfits with the shorts, long white socks and ballet flats on men who are supposedly at the height of their status in the society that the movie is trying to represent? The ultimate fashion dont's on constant display.
Bile-inducing to look at.

Like, WHO are watching these shows and for what purposes? Educational purposes? Puh-lease, that's such a male fantasy.

It's so against my values as a woman to have to constantly be bombarded with these "accurate historical facts" about real events in history, like, I don't live there?

I am a modern, sexually liberated 21st-century woman who has every right to put herself first and dress however I want.

Begone ugly crinolines and waist-snapping corsets!
Begone tall ugly white-haired wigs (we have hair dyes and blowouts now, honey)!
And begone stinky, fully dressed handsome men!

Unfortunately, as a professional entertainment critic, I'm not free to choose what I watch. But for all of you girlies out there, you can skip the historical dramas.

Watch Love Island instead.

authors.name: Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar
authors.bio: Mercedes Jorimara Fack-Bisbar is an esteemed political commentator, a cultural critic and a lifelong defender of Western civilization. With nearly four decades of experience in public discourse, Mrs. Fack-Bisbar has established herself as one of the nation's most uncompromising voices on matters of politics, morality and the increasingly concerning decline of traditional values.

authors.name: Biddy G. Ossip
authors.bio: Biddy G. Ossip is an influential cultural commentator, entertainment critic and an outspoken advocate for women in the show-biz world. Her sharp commentary has inspired numerous public controversies and online debates-- Miss Ossip has certainly established a repuation for her uncompromising, uncensored observations on celebrity culture, fashion, film and theatre.

authors.name: Thaddeus R. Pinchpenny
authors.bio:
Thaddeus R. Pinchpenny is a distinguished financial commentator, entreprenur and graduate of the exceptionally prestigious Kensington-upon-Thames-upon-Cladbury University. 
He is the driving force behind The National Observer's Economical & Business panel  and Pinchpenny credits his success to hard work, personal sacrifice and an unwavering belief in the free market and is quick to jump upon every opportunity to expand his wealth.

authors.name: Lincoln  Windsor Aircors
authors.bio:
Lincoln Aircors is a respected commentator on aristrocratic affaird, royal traditions and the preservation of society's most distinguished institutions.
With an impressive family lineage, his ancestry can be traced to a distant cousin of a distant relative of a minor member of European royalty. 
Aircors has spent much of his professional career to defend the dignity, privileges and public reputations of the noble and higher class.
His columns explore royal affairs, historical traditions and all the essential pillars of social hierachy.
